title: Taito Kato’s Monza Weekend Debrief
excerpt:
Taito Kato and ART Grand Prix were back on form in Monza, achieving two podium finishes across the weekend.

The Japanese driver took his maiden victory in the Sprint Race, after starting in ninth, and followed that up with a run to third in the Feature.

Speaking at the end of it all, Kato reflected on a positive few days at the Temple of Speed…

DOUBLE PODIUM RESULT

“I feel amazing, it’s just incredible. Obviously last couple rounds we were missing pace, the pure pace was just missing.

“It was quite a bit frustrating for me and the team as well. So, this means a lot to be honest. Yesterday was an amazing race for me. Start from P9 to victory. I knew there would be a lot of opportunity in Monza.

Kato was delighted to return to form after a tough few rounds with his team

“But for sure I had everything under control and then finally getting the win and my first ever in the Formula 3, feels amazing.

“Then back-to-back podiums as well is amazing. Today was more tough for me. The pace was missing I would say. But I still managed a podium, so still happy with the result overall. It was one of the most difficult races.”

READ MORE

Ugochukwu on ‘full attack’ in Madrid title fight after impressive fightback in Monza

Lacorte revels in ‘special’ Feature Race victory at home in Monza

THE BACK AND FORTH NATURE OF THE RACES

“It was a bit more chaotic in the race. I was driving in P2 but then a few corners later I would be P4 or P5. Every time on the straight, three-wide on the track, it was a crazy race. But really fun to drive in the car, really enjoyable in the race.

“I was trying to keep everything under control myself. I was able to stay calm for the race and for the weekend as well. There's a lot of positive things in the race weekend, so let's keep going for next round as well.”

Kato is keen to round out the season in style at the final round in madrid

SIXTH IN THE CHAMPIONSHIP AND GOING TO MADRID

“I didn't focus too much on the championship. I just want to focus on the one race, and take it race-by-race.

“Each race I will just focus on my performance then let's see at end of the season. Hopefully we can end with a smile on my face.

“I think we have good confidence in Madrid because we were quite quick in the Madrid test, so I think there will be a good opportunity to fight at the front.”

title: Ugochukwu on ‘full attack’ in Madrid title fight after impressive fightback in Monza
excerpt:
Ugo Ugochukwu went from the back of the field to P8 in the Monza Feature Race and has now set his sights on the final round in Madrid where he is going for the title

Ugo Ugochukwu put in a stunning fightback performance in the Monza Feature Race, recovering from being spun around in the early exchanges to finish in the points.

It was a strong end to what had been a difficult weekend for the Campos Racing driver, starting with an incident in Free Practice that saw him get a five-place grid penalty for both races.

After finishing 10th in the Group A in qualifying, Ugochukwu was forced to start from the back of the field, but his form started to turn around in the races.

The American ended up P13 in the Sprint, and he made a great start in the Feature Race before teammate Théophile Nael made slight contact with the rear of Ugochukwu’s car.

This spun the 19-year-old around and dropped him to the back of the field. However, he continued his fightback, making several overtakes to finish eighth.

“I feel pretty good after today,” he said. “Obviously, you saw the weekend was really tricky, so these four points are quite important for us for the championship.

Ugochukwu went from the back of the field after being spun to the points

“Quali just made things a lot more difficult. We had a little unfortunate incident at Practice, so it wasn't a clean Friday overall. Eyes forward now on Madrid. Race pace was good again today, which is a positive.

“I was not expecting to finish in the points after the little incident in the second lap. To get a few points is nice, but eyes forward on Madrid. Go full attack and finish the season well.”

Speaking more about the incident with Nael, Ugochukwu said was it was an “unfortunate” moment, especially as they had been working together to come through the field as a team.

READ MORE

Lacorte revels in ‘special’ Feature Race victory at home in Monza

FEATURE RACE: Sensational Lacorte takes emotional maiden victory on home soil

“We were planning to work a bit together as well as a team,” he said. “But it was just a little unfortunate kind of tap which got me around. I'm happy I didn't give up because, like I said, those four points were important.

“To be fair, it was quite a fun race. I'm going to come through and make some good moves.”

When asked for his favourite overtake, Ugochukwu responded: “There was one where I think I got four or five people before braking at T1.

Ugochukwu is excited to go to Madrid for the final round of the season

“I towed one guy, then got to the slipstream of another guy, and then got to the slipstream of another guy, and then I managed to pull out right at the end of the straight.

“It was pretty fun. I think always in Monza, the races here are super good, and it's just about how you place your car to maximise as best as you can.”

READ MORE

Round 8 Post-Feature Race Thoughts of the Top Three

‘I love these kinds of races’ – David on going from 17th to fourth in Monza Sprint

Ugochukwu heads to Madrid 17 points behind Freddie Slater in the title fight, with the TRIDENT driver having retired with an issue from pole, he acknowledges that luck was on their side on Sunday.

“I think the result today was a little bit more on our side,” he said. “We have to take it, but for sure in Madrid we need to be making our own luck and be more on the forefront. I'm really confident going into it.

“I had a good feeling at the in-season test the other week. I think the pace was really strong, so I'll try to have a clean Friday. Quali will be important there, and I'm sure it's going to be a good fight for the championship.”

Next Up

title: Lacorte revels in ‘special’ Feature Race victory at home in Monza
excerpt:
Nicola Lacorte paid tribute to his DAMS Lucas Oil team after claiming his and their first victory in FIA Formula 3 – the Italian winning the Monza Feature Race in phenomenal style.

The Pisa, Italy native had a tremendous weekend at the Temple of Speed, starting off on Friday, when he qualified third.

Lacorte followed that up with a run to P9 in the Sprint Race, before storming to victory on Sunday.

Speaking in the paddock after the celebrations, the 19-year-old could hardly believe the history he had made – becoming the first Italian F3 driver to win in Monza.

“It feels great, first podium actually for me, first win in a feature race, that feels amazing,” he said. “It's a great result for the team as well, we've had a really tough couple of seasons, but it all paid off.

“What we've done so far is great and I will always wish this team the best. Of course, it's great to win here as an Italian, I heard I'm the first one to do it, so it's even more special and I feel like it's just the first one of many.”

Lacorte could not be caught once he took the lead of the race

It was not the easiest start to the race for Lacorte, who lost a few places in the opening few laps before fighting back through to take the lead.

Once the DAMS driver got to the front, he could not be caught and he talked through his mindset throughout it all.

READ MORE

FEATURE RACE: Sensational Lacorte takes emotional maiden victory on home soil

Round 8 Post-Feature Race Thoughts of the Top Three

“I knew the race was going to be long,” said Lacorte. “I had a good launch from the grid, the guys did a really good job to fix the clutch from yesterday and it really helped us.

“The start itself was good, then I tried to manage as much as I could in the first laps, because the race was going to be long. As I said, and it actually paid off to manage at the beginning, to have more potential at the end.

“The moves were really precise, it was crucial not to make mistakes at this point, and the pace at the end was just amazing.

Lacorte was delighted to claim his and DAMS' first win in F3

“I was really working well on the exits, to make their life as hard as possible and to help myself. I just did everything I needed to do, everything I could to breathe as much as I could in this race. That is the goal in Monza, and it turned out pretty well.”

DAMS and Lacorte have been a package deal in F3, with the pair having joined forces in 2025 for both their rookie seasons in the Championship.

So to celebrate their first win in the category together at his home race is a memory Lacorte says he will cherish for a long time.

READ MORE

‘I love these kinds of races’ – David on going from 17th to fourth in Monza Sprint

Round 8 Post Sprint Race Press Conference

“We have struggled a lot, especially last year,” he added. “We never had the pace to fight at the front. This year, we have shown great potential from Australia.

“Of course, there was a bit of up and downs in the season, and in the end, the work we've done was great. Everything was good from the team this weekend. I can't thank them enough for this result.

“It was a big party in the garage at the end. I really enjoyed it. To celebrate with the team such a good result was the best way to end the weekend.”

title: Colnaghi and Gladysz penalized following Monza Qualifying session
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of FIA Formula 3 Qualifying at Monza, two drivers have been handed penalties.

Firstly, Mattia Colnaghi has been handed a grid penalty.

The MP Motorsport driver was summoned to the Stewards after an alleged unsafe release during the session.

The Stewards examined the incident and heard from the driver and team representative, and determined that Car 7 had been released into the path of Car 1, Campos Racing’s Theophile Nael in an unsafe manner.

As a result, the Stewards awarded a three-place grid penalty to Colnaghi. The MP driver will serve the penalty in both the Sprint and Feature Races at Monza.

Additionally, Maciej Gladysz has also been handed a grid penalty.

The ART Grand Prix driver was alleged to have been involved in an unsafe release during Qualifying, a potential breach of Article 28.12 (a) of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.

Following the session, the Stewards examined the incident and heard from both the driver and team representative. They determined that Car 11 had been released into the path of Car 5, TRIDENT’s Freddie Slater in an unsafe manner.

As a result, they applied a three-place grid penalty to the ART driver. Gladysz will serve the penalty in both the Sprint and Feature Race this weekend.

Finally, Car 1 of Nael and Car 25 of Jin Nakamura have been given permission to start both races this weekend after failing to set a time within 107% in Qualifying.

Both drivers will start from the back of the grid after the application of any other penalties in accordance with Article 34.2 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.

title: Bhirombhakdi penalised following Monza Feature Race
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of the FIA Formula 3 Feature Race at Monza, Nandhavud Bhirombhakdi has been penalised.

The Thai driver was alleged to have driven erratically during the Feature Race. Afterwards, the Stewards examined CCTV video evidence, heard from the driver and DAMS Lucas Oil team representative.

They determined that Car 30 had driven on track in the opposite direction while another car had been approaching in the correct direction of travel at Turns 1 and 2.

This constitutded a breach of Article 27.4 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. As a result, the Stewards applied a 10-second stop-and-go penalty. With the penalty assessed post-race, the penalty is applied as a 30-second time penalty.

With the additional 30 seconds applied, Bhirombhadki drops from 18th to 23rd in the Monza Feature Race classification.

title: Round 8 Post-Feature Race Thoughts of the Top Three
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Nicola Lacorte, F3 Feature Race winner at Monza, how does that sound?

Nicola Lacorte: It sounds crazy, especially because it's here in Monza, at my home race. So it feels even more special. But I expected to have a really good result today. Of course, winning is something even more special. So it's gratifying.

FIA Formula 3: Let's talk about the race, you started from P3, and then the start was not that great if memory serves.

Lacorte: I mean, the launch was really good. I couldn't manage to fight Freddie and Kanato, because T1 is very tight, and I tried to bring the car to the end. I knew it was going to be a long race. So I just put myself behind, managed, got overtaken if it was needed, and then overtook back. And I think it was the perfect strategy. Combined with the management on the tyres, there was quite a lot of graining. I didn't expect it to be that early, but I managed to clean it quite quickly to get rid of it. It was good at the end.

FIA Formula 3: When you got into the lead, how difficult was it to actually keep it and also, when it was the final lap towards the chequered flag, what went through your mind?

Lacorte: So when I got into the lead, I thought it was going to be just for a couple of laps, because the tow and the DRS here is very strong. But actually, I kept it for quite a long time. When it was a Safety Car, I cooled down a bit, and I started to think. It was a bit of a problem, because you shouldn't think at this point of the race. Then I got back in the mindset, and I was just going corner by corner, looking at how to get more and more of a gap with good exits. When I saw the chequered flag, I just had no words. I screamed in the helmet, opened the radio and then after a couple of corners, I couldn't speak. So of course, it's a great emotion. I just want to keep this momentum up I started in Hungary, and it's just getting better now.

FIA Formula 3: What does it mean for you to give DAMS their first ever Feature Race win?

Lacorte: I think they deserve it a lot, because we came here with no experience two years ago. I wasn't ready for F3. I knew it. The team struggled a bit. It was normal. I expected it. They trusted in me, and I trusted in them, and we just built the performance of today, race by race, lap by lap. I think it just proves how strong we are, and that we can challenge the more experienced teams in this category.

FIA Formula 3: There's one final round next week at Madrid, at a new track, with more points to grab. Two Qualifying sessions, two Feature Races, and one Sprint. What's the objective? How are you going to approach that weekend?

Lacorte: Same as always. Like I started this weekend, just be fast in Practice, be fast in the quali, and then see how it goes. It has to be corner by corner, lap by lap, session by session. I'll just keep the same mindset. It was tough testing for us in Madrid, so we just need to work more and get the best out of it. I'm sure we can get good satisfaction again.

FIA Formula 3: Well, massive congratulations on today's result. Tuukka Tappanen, P2 in today's Feature Race. Back on the podium, some strong points. Dare I say finally?

Tuukka Taponen: Yes, you can say finally. It's been a very tough year, especially at the beginning of the season. A few rounds ago we found some pace and since that we have been fighting at the front. Luck has not been on our side. Three punctures in two races has ruined a lot of points. But finally, starting from P8 and finishing in P2 is a very good result. The team is really deserving that. We have been fighting with the result to get the result and finally we get it.

FIA Formula 3: Like you said, from P8 on the grid to P2 at the flag. It was very hectic everywhere, but especially at the front. How did you manage that?

Taponen: It was quite hectic. I was going forward all the time. It was quite good for me with the fights. Just at the end we started to get that front graining. It was very difficult to get close to the car in front. We didn't have the DRS because there was a yellow flag in Turn 1. It didn't really help to fight for the win, but I have to be happy for P2 as well.

FIA Formula 3: Now there is one final round and it is going to be a super-sized one at Madrid. At a new track, obviously F3 has had the privilege to be testing there a couple of weeks ago. What are you expecting from that final round of the season?

Taponen: Let's hope that it will be clean in Qualifying and we can drive a decent session. I think it's super important in Madrid because overtaking is very difficult.

FIA Formula 3: What is the target to conclude 2026?

Taponen: The objective is to keep going with this momentum that we have had for a few rounds already. And then convert it to good results.

FIA Formula 3: Thank you very much, good job today. Taito Kato, P3 in today's Feature Race here at Monza. Second podium, back-to-back after yesterday's win. What an amazing result for you this weekend.

Taito Kato: Yeah, really strong weekend overall. I'm happy for me and the team. Just massive thanks to the team. ART were preparing quite a lot. just using the simulator and making sure we had a good setup. We found it, and today's race was much more tough compared to yesterday. On pure pace, we were losing a little bit compared to the two guys in front but still managed it. Back-to-back races on the podium. Still happy with the result with strong points in the back. I can't wait for the next round.

FIA Formula 3: You've mentioned it being a tough race. It looked fun from the outside but obviously it must have been really difficult from inside the car. How tricky was it to stay out of trouble?

Kato: Yeah, obviously yesterday was the same. Quite chaotic overall in the race. Three wide on the straight, four wide on the straight. But I was always staying calm inside the car. Just staying focused, saving the tyres because today was a bit cooler temperature-wise and the issue was the graining for front. I think everyone had massive graining as well. So I think I should have been tyre-saving more in the beginning. But still managed it. So happy with the result.

FIA Formula 3: It's an amazing result for you and ART here in Monza. There's no rest, we're going straight to Madrid where it's going to be a very tough weekend again. A new track that you discovered with testing, but with two qualifying sessions and then two Feature Races and a Sprint Race. How are you going to go into the weekend?

Kato: I think we were able to do good testing in Madrid. We were fighting at the front. So we have confidence with the car. And also, I think it's a good opportunity to gain points in the two Feature Races and one Sprint Race. So, yes, no rest time. But we will do the maximum performance for Madrid.

FIA Formula 3: Thank you very much, congratulations.

title: FEATURE RACE: Sensational Lacorte takes emotional maiden victory on home soil
excerpt:
Nicola Lacorte put in an outstanding performance to take victory on home soil at the Monza Feature Race, DAMS Lucas Oil’s first in the FIA Formula 3 Championship.

The Italian came through from P3 to take the lead and could not be caught once he did. Lacorte went on to win ahead of MP Motorsport’s Tuukka Taponen and Taito Kato for ART Grand Prix.

In the title fight, Freddie Slater retired with an issue, while Ugo Ugochukwu went from the back of the field to eighth, with 15 points now separating the top two going to the final round in Madrid.

AS IT HAPPENED

It was a great start for polesitter Slater, while Kanato Le held Lacorte off in the opening few corners to maintain second place.

Behind them, Ernesto Rivera overtook Kato for P5, with Alessandro Giusti right on the back of the Sprint Race winner.

Further back, Ugochukwu was spun around at Turn 1 after being hit in the rear by Campos Racing teammate Théophile Nael. This dropped the American from P19 to P29.

With the DRS activated, Le was right on the back of Slater on Lap 3, but the Safety Car halted his hopes of an overtake. Fionn McLaughlin collided with Nandhavud Bhirombhakdi at the opening corner, bringing an end to the Hitech driver’s race.

Racing resumed on Lap 5 and Slater led the field away, with Kato going around the outside of Lacorte at Turn 1 to take P4. Pedro Clerot then did the same move on Taponen for P7.

ART were flying once again, as Le used the DRS to get ahead of Slater. Kato then did the same on Rivera for P3, with Lacorte following him through.

The Championship leader lost a lot of time to Le, and going into the Roggia chicane, Kato took second place from him, as Lacorte relegated him to fourth a few corners later.

Campos’ day was going from bad to worse as Rivera, having hit the rear of Lacorte at the Ascari chicane, had a damaged front wing, with the team bringing him in on Lap 8.

Slater led the pack in the early stages but his race then unravelled and he eventually retired

Lacorte was now the driver on the move, overtaking Kato for second, and closing the gap to Le to 0.7s. Slater’s struggles continued as Taponen got ahead of the TRIDENT at Turn 1.

On to Lap 9, and Nael was given a 10-second time penalty for the incident with Ugochukwu. Moments later, he came into the pitlane to change a damaged front wing after hitting the rear of Noah Stromsted at the second chicane.

Lap 10 saw another change for the lead as Lacorte took P1 from Le, with Kato then relegating his teammate to P3 at Turn 1.

Taponen was next to charge through, as he made a double overtake on Le and Kato to get up to second. His MP teammate Alessandro Giusti then overtook Slater down the main straight, with Hiyu Yamakoshi relegating the TRIDENT to seventh.

In the title fight, the British driver was on the radio saying he had to retire the car with an issue, as Ugochukwu, having been spun to the back of the field, was up to P14 at the start of Lap 13.

The American gained a position after Jin Nakamura ran through the gravel and spun at the final corner. The hitech driver was able to continue on but dropped to P22.

Slater’s fears of an issue were true as his rear right tyre came off at the Ascari chicane, causing him to stop on track. Rivera also parked his car at Turn 1 with an issue. With both cars needing to be cleared, the Safety Car was brought out.

Racing was back underway on Lap 17 as the leading drivers maintained position, while Ugochukwu gained two places, going from 13th to 11th – and on the edge of the points.

Lacorte had done a great job, as he was 0.7s clear of Taponen, who was 1.4s ahead of Kato going on to Lap 18.

Yevan David was once again flying and got up to fifth at Parabolica after overtaking Giusti at the final corner.

Lacorte kept Taponen at a distance to claim his maiden F3 win for DAMS Lucas Oil

Ugochukwu was into the top 10 on Lap 20, overtaking Enzo Deligny, while Lacorte was 0.9s clear of Taponen, with the MP driver struggling to stay within DRS range.

But with Fernando Barrichello having stopped on track at Turn 1, the yellow flags were out, with the DRS now disabled.

On to the final lap, and Taponen was struggling to reel in Lacorte, as David overtook Le for P4 at the final corner.

But at the front, it was a first FIA Formula 3 victory for Lacorte – who became the first Italian to win on home soil and the 13th different winner of the season to set a new F3 record.

Taponen achieved MP’s first podium of the season in P2, while Kato followed up his Sprint victory with a third place. David was fourth ahead of Le, with Yamakoshi sixth ahead of Stromsted.

Ugochukwu put in a sublime drive from last to finish in eighth, as Deligny took P9 ahead of James Wharton.

KEY QUOTE – Nicola Lacorte, DAMS Lucas Oil

“I knew I was going to be fast here in Monza but I didn’t expect to win. The race was just perfect, good pace, that’s we deserve, since the beginning of the year, to show what the team and I are capable of.”

CHAMPIONSHIP STANDINGS

Freddie Slater continues to lead the Drivers’ Championship on 141 points, while Ugo Ugochukwu closes the deficit in second, going onto 126 points. In third is Ernesto Rivera with 76 points, one ahead of teammate Théophile Nael while Brando Badoer and Taito Kato are level on points in fifth and sixth places with 71 apiece.

In the Teams’ Standings, Campos Racing remain at the top with 277 ahead of TRIDENT with 213. ART Grand Prix and Van Amersfoort Racing are level on 155 points, while MP Motorsport complete the top five with 131.

UP NEXT

The drivers will now head to Madrid for the final round of the season, with the Spanish venue hosting an extra race from September 11-13.

title: Several drivers penalized following Monza Sprint Race
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of the FIA Formula 3 Sprint Race, several drivers have been handed post-race penalties.

Firstly, Brando Badoer has been handed a 10-second time penalty for forcing another driver off circuit.

During the race, the Rodin Motorsport driver was involved in a collision with Car 28, AIX Racing’s Fernando Barrichello, with the pair making contact on the start/finish straight after a defensive move towards the AIX driver.

After the race, the Stewards heard from both drivers and team representatives along with examining video evidence. They determined that Badoer’s defensive block on Barrichello had come too late, and that the Italian driver forced the AIX car off circuit in the process.

As a result, the Stewards applied a 10-second time penalty to the Rodin driver. With the penalty applied, Badoer finishes P23 in the Sprint classification.

Additionally, Barrichello has been handed a time penalty.

The AIX Racing driver was judged to have made an unsafe re-entry to the track in the lead up to the contact with Badoer.

As a result, the Stewards elected to apply a five-second time penalty to the Brazilian. With the AIX driver failing to finish the Sprint Race, his time penalty is converted into a grid drop of three positions.

Barrichello will serve the penalty in the Monza Feature Race.

Secondly, James Wharton has been handed a post-race penalty.

The PREMA Racing driver was involved in a collision with ART Grand Prix’s Kanato Le during the Sprint.

After the race, the Stewards heard from both drivers, PREMA and ART team representatives and examined video evidence.

They determined that Car 21 had been wholly responsible for the collision, making a sudden move right, leading to the contact with Le.

With the penalty applied, Wharton is now classified 21st in the Sprint Race results.

Next, Ricardo Escotto has been handed a time penalty for causing a collision.

The AIX Racing driver was alleged to have made contact with Car 18 of Badoer during the Sprint Race. Aftewards, the Stewards heard from both drivers, team representatives and examined video evidence.

They determined that Car 26 was wholly responsible for the contact between the two Cars at Turn 2. As a result, they elected to apply a 10-second time penalty to Escotto.

With the application of his penalty, Escotto is now classified P22 in the Sprint Race.

Finally, Gerrard Xie has been awarded a 10-second time penalty.

During the race, the DAMS Lucas Oil driver was involved in an incident with Hitech driver Woohyun Shin at the first corner that put both drivers out of the race.

Following the Sprint, the Stewards heard from both drivers and their team representatives, and examined video evidence.

They determined that Car 31 was wholly responsible for the collision, and as a result, applied a 10-second time penalty to the Chinese driver.

With Xie failing to finish the Sprint Race, his time penalty is instead converted into a grid drop of 10 places. The DAMS driver will serve the penalty in the Monza Feature Race.

title: Round 8 Post Sprint Race Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 3 press conference following the Sprint Race here at Monza. Joining us in third place from Van Amersfoort Racing is Hiyu Yamakoshi. In second place from TRIDENT is Freddie Slater. Also joining us from ART Grand Prix, having captured his first FIA Formula 3 win, is Taito Kato. Taito, congratulations on your first FIA Formula 3 win. How does that feel?

Taito Kato: It feels amazing. It is incredible. I am speechless, to be honest, after starting from P9. I knew there would be good opportunities to overtake here at Monza. The car was amazing throughout the race and really enjoyable to drive. A massive thank you to my team because the car was incredible. We struggled a little with performance over the last couple of races, so I am very happy with this result.

FIA Formula 3: There were a few Safety Cars today. How were you able to execute with so much happening around you?

Kato: I saw the chaos in front, especially at the beginning when cars were three or four wide on the straight. I stayed calm throughout the race, avoided incidents and managed the tyres. The pace looked really good and I felt confident throughout, so I always stayed calm inside the car.

FIA Formula 3: You mentioned staying calm inside the car. Can you take us through the final laps? It did not look as though you put a foot wrong.

Kato: The pace was good and the car was incredible. I knew that if I did not make a mistake, I could win the race. That was why I stayed focused.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on the victory.

Kato: Thank you.

FIA Formula 3: Freddie, congratulations. That is your eighth podium of the season. You went from P12 to P2. Tell us how you were able to do it.

Freddie Slater: It was a pretty chaotic race. During the first few laps there were not many opportunities and I think I only gained one or two positions. Then the momentum kept going. I knew the key to racing at Monza was to keep moving forward because, as soon as you go backwards, it is very difficult to reset. A lot of people made mistakes and there were several incidents ahead. I knew I needed to bide my time because it was a long race and the tow and DRS are so powerful. I used that to my advantage and came through the field. It was a very positive race from my side, and the team gave me an amazing car. It is one I will remember for a long time because it was good fun.

FIA Formula 3: You made some incredible moves, especially into the first chicane. Can you take us through some of those? There was one where you were on the grass.

Slater: That was not ideal. I did not fancy mowing the grass at Monza. We were four wide and the slipstream was so powerful that all three of us were arriving together, so it was always going to happen. It probably looked spectacular on television, but in the car it felt manageable. When you are four wide, nobody knows exactly where everyone else is. I tried to get back onto the track, managed to do so and then picked the move off at the end to come away with P2.

FIA Formula 3: You have also extended your lead in the Drivers' Championship. What is your mindset heading into Sunday's Feature Race?

Slater: It is the same approach: try to score as many points as possible in every race, achieve a good result and execute as we have done all year. Another podium is special. We have a very good team behind me that gives me a car with which I can be consistent. It is now my job to execute and pick up the pieces.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations, Freddie. Great drive . FIA Formula 3: Hiyu, another great drive and your third podium of the season. How does this one feel?

Hiyu Yamakoshi: It feels like a progression from fourth to third. I had a difficult time, but the goal before the start was to maintain position and fight at the front. In the end, the team and I managed it quite well. From the first round, I felt I did not have as much pace as others, so I tried to maximise what I had. This podium is special, particularly because of how difficult the pace was and how we managed the race.

FIA Formula 3: Like Freddie and Taito, you had to fight through the field. How challenging was it to navigate everything that was happening?

Yamakoshi: This time I was thinking a lot, although I also had good luck and was able to drive through much of what happened. We had considered many options and simulations about what could happen and how much pace we would have. The preparation through those simulations helped us achieve this result.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on P3.

Yamakoshi: Thank you very much.

title: ‘I love these kinds of races’ – David on going from 17th to fourth in Monza Sprint
excerpt:
Yevan David reflected on his incredible race in the Monza Sprint that saw him go from P17 to fourth place

Yevan David hailed his “incredible” drive from P17 to fourth place in the Monza Sprint, with the AIX Racing driver aiming to do even better in Sunday’s Feature Race.

The Sri Lankan had an excellent morning, steadily making moves through the field, before making a final lap overtake at the last corner on Alessandro Giusti to take P4.

Reflecting on the race, David admitted he knew such a performance was possible given that they had not shown their true pace in Qualifying – where he finished 10th in Group B.

“Honestly it was incredible,” said David on the race. “I knew we had the pace and the potential, we just got a bit unlucky in qualifying but it happens. I knew it was Monza and I was being a bit careful in the first lap.

“Luckily, I made a couple of positions and then from that point onwards was just keeping it clean. We obviously gained a lot of positions just from people crashing and the unfortunate incidents. I was able to make quite a few overtakes, especially on the last lap with Sandro into the last corner.

David made his way through the field from P17 to P4 in the Monza Sprint Race

“So that was a really nice one for me to get P4. Obviously, it would have been nice to be on the podium, a few more laps and we probably would have been. But that's the goal for tomorrow to be up there again.

“It's really nice to score points, I really like Monza. It's a little bit of a home race for me. I've got some family here, I lived here for a while as well. So honestly it was a really nice experience.”

Speaking more about the race, David revealed what his game plan was, as he set his sights on overtaking those in front while also defending from others, with there being three DRS zones around the lap.

READ MORE

SPRINT RACE: Kato flies through for maiden victory as Slater extends championship lead

QUALIFYING: Impressive Slater takes pole with title rival Ugochukwu down the order in Monza

“I think mentally I was always trying to keep calm because it's a long race,” he said. Technically, I was just really trying to focus on getting a good exit.

“The momentum down these straights is very important, and also so is getting a good exit compared to the people behind that have DRS.

“So I was really just focused on that and I knew even though I didn't have DRS to the guys in front, they'll fight a little bit. Then if I kept consistent, I'll get the DRS and make some moves. So it's just about remaining calm, focusing on exits for the momentum on the straights.”

The AIX driver is setting his sights on an even better Sunday in Italy

With plenty of action and overtakes out on track, David continued to talk about his appreciation for Monza, and the challenges the Temple of Speed presents drivers.

“Honestly, I'm a driver that can't emphasise this enough,” he continued. “Obviously, it's not nice to see people crashing and incidents like that. But to just have close racing and battles from Lap 1 to Lap 18, honestly, I couldn't have enjoyed it more.

READ MORE

PRACTICE: Giusti leads strong MP Motorsport 1-2-3 at Monza opener

Round 8 Post Qualifying Press Conference

“I just love being in such a mix like that. I love these kind of races. It's what I'm here for. That's the best part of racing for me. So, I honestly really loved it and hope Monza is going to be on the calendar for eternity, to be honest.”

Looking ahead to the Feature Race, David says he is aiming to have an even better race on Sunday, even though he would not be drawn on what result he is targeting.

“Well, I'm not results orientated,” he concluded. “But let's say I'm aiming for an even better race.”

title: SPRINT RACE: Kato flies through for maiden victory as Slater extends championship lead
excerpt:
Taito Kato went from ninth to the top step of the podium in the Monza Sprint Race, putting in a phenomenal performance to claim his first victory in FIA Formula 3.

The ART Grand Prix driver had to hold off TRIDENT’s Freddie Slater, who went from P12 to second, on the final lap to claim victory.

The Championship leader extends his advantage to 17 points, with rival Ugo Ugochukwu finishing in P14. Van Amersfoort Racing’s Hiyu Yamakoshi took the final spot on the podium in third.

AS IT HAPPENED

It was a good start from the Rodin Motorsport front row as Brando Badoer and Pedro Clerot worked together to keep Tuukka Taponen in P3 in the opening few corners.

Behind them, Alessandro Giusti made a good start to get ahead of Fernando Barrichello for P4.

Badoer had done a good job to break the tow to his teammate but locked up into Turn 1 on Lap 2, allowing Clerot to close in on the run to the Roggia chicane.

The Italian’s scruffy second lap continued at the exit of the Ascari chicane, where he ran wide, with his teammate then taking the lead going into the final corner.

Taponen then went to the inside of Badoer at Parabolica to take P2 on Lap 4, but as they went down the main straight, the top five were battling for the lead.

Barrichello, Badoer and Taponen then made contact on the run to Turn 1. The latter two made it back into the pitlane with front wing damage before dropping to the rear of the field.

As for Barrichello, he stopped on track with rear suspension damage, bringing out the Safety Car. In all of this, Giusti took the lead ahead of Clerot with Rivera up to third ahead of Kato.

Racing resumed on Lap 7 of 18, and it was an excellent restart from Giusti, as Kato went around the outside of Rivera at Turn 1 for P3.

It was a great start from the Brando Badoer and Pedro Clerot for Rodin

Mattia Colnaghi was also on the move getting past Yamakoshi for P5 at the opening corner.

The Argentinian driver then locked up into Turn 1 on the next lap, and went through the runoff area, dropping him down to P8. Slater’s steady charge saw him up in sixth ahead of James Wharton.

The Virtual Safety Car was soon signalled with Maciej Gladysz having stopped on track, but with his ART car cleared, racing continued on Lap 9.

Clerot had a great restart and took the lead from Giusti into Turn 3, while Yamakoshi found the door shut by Rivera at the same corner.

Giusti’s tough lap continued with Kato taking P2 from him on the run to Parabolica. The French driver did retake the position down the main straight which soon turned into the lead as Clerot stopped on track with an issue.

The Safety Car was back out with Gerrard Xie and Woohyun Shin having also made contact at Turn 1. Both drivers were out the car and ok.

Giusti led the field away on Lap 14 with all three cars cleared, with Rivera running wide at Turn 1 after a battle with Kato for P3. Slater took advantage of this to take fourth position from the Campos.

In the battle for the final points paying positions, Enzo Deligny went around the outside of Wharton for P8 at the Ascari chicane, although the PREMA driver took back the place.

It was a tough few corners for Giusti, who went from the lead to fourth, after losing out to Kato and Yamakoshi. Slater then went around the outside of the MP driver for P3 at Turn 1, despite a brief run on the grass and slight contact between the two.

The Championship leader was flying and was up to second after making a move past Yamakoshi at the final corner, although the Van Amersfoort Racing driver retook the place at Turn 1.

ART then came on the radio to tell Kato to give it everything on the penultimate lap, and he obliged as he kept the lead going onto the final tour.

The top three celebrate on the podium at the end of the race

Slater and Giusti then went past Yamakoshi into Turn 1, although the VAR driver was able to retake P3 from the Frenchman a few corners later.

The TRIDENT driver was putting a lot of pressure on Kato, but the ART driver held on to take his first win in Formula 3, with Slater going from P12 to second, as Yamakoshi rounded out the podium.

Yevan David made a final lap overtake on Giusti for P4, with Colnaghi recovering to sixth ahead of Rivera. Deligny finished eighth, ahead of Nicola Lacorte as Bruno del Pino rounded out the top 10.

KEY QUOTE – Taito Kato, ART Grand Prix

“This means a lot because the last couple of races we were quite struggling with the performance. It was quite frustrating for me and for the team as well, and then to finally ne back on the podium for the first time since Melbourne.

“So it’s quite a long time ago. But I still remember how to drive to the win. It’s incredible. I’m speechless. The car was amazing all the race. I just want to say thank you to my team and my engineers, my mechanics, all the fans. It's a lot of effort. There is a lot of support to me, and I’m really grateful to drive in Monza.”

CHAMPIONSHIP STANDINGS

Freddie Slater moves to 139 points and extends his championship lead over Ugo Ugochukwu to 17 points going into the Feature Race. Ernesto Rivera is up to third on 76 points with Théophile Nael a point behind in fourth. Brando Badoer stays fifth with 71 points.

In the Teams’ Standings, Campos Racing retain their lead on 273 points with TRIDENT second on 207. Van Amersfoort Racing are third on 144 points, with ART Grand Prix jump up to fourth on 130, as Rodin Motorsport round out the top five on 121.

UP NEXT

The drivers get one more chance to claim victory at the Temple of Speed, with lights out for the Feature Race set for 08:15 local time on Sunday.

title: Matteo De Palo disqualified from Monza Qualifying
excerpt:
Matteo De Palo has been disqualified from the Monza Qualifying session for a technical infringement.

Car 6 was referred to the Stewards by the FIA Technical Delegate after it was found that the height of the diffuser on the TRIDENT car was below the required minimum height as laid out in Article 3.4.1a of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations.

The part in question was measured 3mm lower than the stipulated height in the Regulations on the left-hand side.

Having received the Technical Report, the Stewards heard from a TRIDENT team representative and determined that the height of the diffuser was below the minimum stipulated height without justifiable cause.

As a result, Car 6 was disqualified in line with the standard penalty for a technical infringement.

title: Round 8 Post Qualifying Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Welcome, everyone, to today's FIA Formula 3 press conference following qualifying here at Monza. Joining us in P3 from DAMS Lucas Oil is Nicola Lacorte, in second place, from TRIDENT, is Matteo De Palo; and also from TRIDENT, capturing his third pole of the season, is Freddie Slater. Freddie, congratulations. You only had one lap to do it. How challenging was it?

Freddie Slater: Yes, definitely very challenging. Obviously, this morning we had, I think, around 30-degree track temperature, and this afternoon it was 55, so there was a big swing in track conditions and definitely a different balance. The team had to give us a car that could be in the window. At the end of the day, we had one lap to deliver, and we did the job and got nice track position as well. I'm very happy with the job we did, and I look forward to the weekend.

FIA Formula 3: Coming back to that track position, how did you and the team plan for it? It did look like the tow was pretty strong out there today.

Slater: Giacomo, the Team Manager, did a really good job, honestly. Hats off to him for what he did. He had all the situations covered. He kept me up to date with how much margin we had, whether we could do two push laps or one push lap, and the sequence. The run plan was changing every minute, every second. Hats off to the team for being calm under pressure and giving me the opportunity to go out there and do what I do. From then on, it was my job to put in a clean lap, in a good position with a good tow, and hopefully get pole at the end of the day.

FIA Formula 3: Were the tyres quite tricky out there today? Could you get more than one push lap out of them?

Slater: I think so, but we only did one, so we'll never know. We also only did one out-lap, which is not always normal. It was straight out into a first push, which is not easy for drivers, especially when you have a corner like Turn 1 as the first braking zone. It definitely wasn't easy for anyone, and it all came down to execution.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on the pole position. Matteo, coming to you, congratulations on P2. How does that feel?

Matteo De Palo: It feels good. It was a good lap. It was not an easy session for me either. We didn't have many laps, so only one counted, and it was the right one. Positioning was really tricky, but, as Freddie said, it was well managed for me as well. I think I was in the right place and then also put together a really good lap. We missed out on overall pole position by three hundredths, so there is everything to play for on Sunday. I'm happy with the work we did today.

FIA Formula 3: It's a front-row lockout for TRIDENT. What does that mean to you and the team?

De Palo: It's always good to start from the front row, especially here in Monza for me and the team, because there is an Italian connection for both of us. It's really nice. Especially for me, coming from some difficult rounds, it feels like redemption because I haven't been able to show many things lately due to circumstances outside my control. So, yes, it's definitely nice.

FIA Formula 3: It's your home race as well. What has the fan atmosphere been like?

De Palo: It's been crazy so far. Yesterday, we had a couple of fan zones, and it was really nice to have everyone here. There were also quite a lot of people at the track today watching us, so it was really good.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations.

De Palo: Thank you very much.

FIA Formula 3: Nicola, coming to you next, congratulations on P3. Can you take me through your lap?

Nicola Lacorte: As Freddie said, we only had one push lap in the end, which was not ideal for the tyres or for what we had planned. Of course, you have to get the most out of it, and that's what the team and I did. I think pole was really difficult today, but we did what we could. My lap started well with a good tow. As you said, it was very powerful. Unfortunately, I finished without a tow because the car in front of me went off, so I was on my own for the rest of the lap. I'm really happy with the pace because it will also be important to have good pace without a tow tomorrow. I think we did a really good job, considering the season so far.

FIA Formula 3: Trying to strike the balance between having the right amount of downforce on the car and also having good straight-line speed, was it challenging to find that balance?

Lacorte: I think the best option is to have a tow, even though you know you're going to lose some downforce in fast corners like the Lesmos and Ascari. You just need to deal with it, get the most out of those fast corners, and take the advantage on the straights.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on P3.

title: QUALIFYING: Impressive Slater takes pole with title rival Ugochukwu down the order in Monza
excerpt:
Freddie Slater took the Aramco Pole Position Award in phenomenal style in Monza, completing a 1:38.114 in Group B to beat TRIDENT teammate Matteo De Palo to the top prize.

De Palo set the pace in Group A with a 1:38.143, where Slater’s title rival Ugo Ugochukwu hit trouble and wound up in P10. The Italian will line up on the front row, while Nicola Lacorte will start in third after finishing second in Group B.

GROUP A

It was a slow start to the session but the drivers started to venture out with five minutes to go.

This gave most of them time for just one flying lap, with Hiyu Yamakoshi fastest on a 1:38.261. Taito Kato was just 0.014s behind but ahead of Fernando Barrichello in P3.

Critically, title contender Ugo Ugochukwu had a wide moment at Turn 1, and as a result ended up. Unfortunately for the Campos Racing driver he had no time to start another lap, having taken the chequered flag.

Matteo De Palo was one of the few who was able to get a second lap, and he went to P1 with a 1:38.143, beating Kanato Le to provisional pole by 0.020s.

Kato wound up third ahead of Yamakoshi and Barrichello, as Tuukka Taponen rounded out the top six.

With the final runs complete, Ugochukwu wound up in P10, leaving him with an uphill task for both races.

GROUP B

De Palo’s 1:38.143 was the time to beat, and just like the previous group, the drivers stayed in the pitlane until the final few minutes of the session.

They all had time for just one flying lap and it was Freddie Slater that shone the brightest with a 1:38.114, beating Nicola Lacorte by 0.236s.

Ernesto Rivera was third ahead of MP Motorsport duo Alessandro Giusti and Mattia Colnaghi as Pedro Clerot rounded out the top six.

Slater’s time was good enough to take pole position ahead of his TRIDENT teammate De Palo, with Lacorte set to start P3.

For Saturday’s Sprint Race, Taponen will start from reverse grid pole, with Clerot joining him on the front row.

That wraps up the Monza action for today, with the drivers set to return to the track tomorrow for the Sprint Race at 09:30 local time.

title: Ugo Ugochukwu handed grid penalty for both Monza races
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of Practice in Monza, Ugo Ugochukwu has been handed a grid penalty for causing a collision.

The Campos Racing driver was alleged to have caused a collision with Car 6 belonging to TRIDENT driver Matteo De Palo.

After the session, the Stewards heard from both drivers and team representatives and examined video evidence.

The Stewards determined that Car 2 had crowded Car 6 off the circuit and was therefore wholly at fault for the collision, breaching Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.

As a result, they applied a five-place grid penalty to the Campos driver. Ugochukwu will serve the penalty in both the Sprint and Feature Races this weekend in Monza.

title: ‘The car is quick’ says Giusti after ending Monza Free Practice on top
excerpt:
Alessandro Giusti reflected on a strong Free Practice session in Monza where he ended up with the fastest time

Alessandro Giusti was fastest in the Monza Free Practice and is hoping for more of the same in Qualifying. However, he does not believe pole position is vital to him having a good weekend in Italy.

The Frenchman’s 1:37.445 was the quickest time of the session, and impressively for MP Motorsport, he led a 1-2-3 for the team with Tuukka Taponen and Mattia Colnaghi in behind.

Speaking in the paddock afterwards, Giusti was impressed by their performance in what he felt was a largely clean session.

“It was good, it was decent,” said Giusti. “We executed well and we did a good lap. We had a good tow and the car is quick so just need the same for quali.

“Everyone wants a tow because in Monza it's nearly not possible to do a good lap without the tow, so everyone wants to have a clear tow and that's what I had.

“It was quite a clean FP but I think quali will be even more messy but I hope it will be safe for everyone and we can all have good laps.”

Giusti ended up with the fastest time in this morning's Monza Free Practice

Giusti set his time with the Soft tyres that they will be using in Qualifying after starting the session on their carry over Hards from the Madrid test.

The Williams Driver Academy member was happy to get a feel for the car on the softer compound going into the pole position shootout later today.

"I think there was quite a big gain on the softer tyre, it was really good,” Giusti continued. “I think the track was quick, and we were easily a second quicker than last year’s FP.

READ MORE

PRACTICE: Giusti leads strong MP Motorsport 1-2-3 at Monza opener

2026 Monza Qualifying Groups Drawn

“I think we will be a bit slower for quali because of the hot temperature, but anyway it doesn't change anything, it will be the same for everyone so we just need to do our job.”

Looking ahead to Qualifying, Giusti is set to run in Group B, and while he says he will be looking for a tow, he feels that getting in a clean lap is more important in the battle for top spot.

“Last year it was not that messy to be honest, everyone got a clean lap,” he said. “I think this year the goal is to have the same quali. It will be easier for everyone but I mean everyone wants a tow of like one or two seconds, something like this.

The French driver is hoping for a clean qualifying session this afternoon

“Around here you don't have so many corners, there is a lot of high speeds, so a good tow is needed, but if it's a mess it's better to do a lap as well.

“So if you had the choice of having a tow but doing no laps and having no tow but doing laps, it would be the second choice, so that's something we need to be good at and we need to look for in quali.”

READ MORE

PREVIEW: All to play for in Round 8 at Monza

‘Determined’ Badoer aiming to maximise performance at ‘special’ home race weekend in Monza

As for his goals in the afternoon session, Giusti acknowledges pole position would be nice, but that around Monza, it is not the be all and end all.

“To get pole would be nice but here it's not the fastest always with pole,” he concludes. “I feel like I just need to be in the good group for the race. Last year the winner never started on the front row, so I mean just start in a good position would be nice.

“I would be happy with a place in the top six but if it's pole for sure we'll take it, it's two points and to do pole in Monza, my origin being a bit Italian, it would be good to get it here, so I'll be happy.”
